## Historical audit — S0284

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_v3/results/historical_r1_C2_start/test/bw_0056/2/trajectory.jsonl`. Citations below refer to this JSONL file. All supplied observations are whole lines, not split observations.

**Goal versus interpretation.** The requested goal was a separate-mesh Blender reconstruction matching one photograph’s viewpoint, framing, objects and materials (line 1, `model_request`). The student interpreted the scene as a cleanroom with two operators and a packaging line; that inventory is a student observation, not independent confirmation of the unseen reference (line 3, `H model_response`).

| Evidence | Observed operation or result |
|---|---|
| Lines 3–4, `H model_response` / `execute` step 1 | Program created named architecture, machine, conveyor, HMI and two person assets with child parts. It specified colored surfaces, translucent guards and metallic/roughness settings, but no image textures. Person limbs and HMI supports were separate positioned primitives; names and hierarchy do not verify physical connections or contact. |
| Lines 6, 8–10, `build_completed`, `render_completed`, `execution_result`, `select` | First build and render succeeded, `ok: true`, and step 1 was selected. The log records a saved image, not its visual accuracy. |
| Lines 11–14, `H model_request` / `model_response` / `execute` step 2 | After receiving the first render, the student reported that the room and floor dominated and people, machine and screen were too small. It moved the camera closer, expanded the room, adjusted figures and equipment, added fixtures and changed lighting. This is the student’s diagnosis, not independent visual verification. |
| Lines 16, 18–20, build/render/result/select | The revised build and render also completed successfully; step 2 was selected. |
| Lines 21, 23–24, `H model_request` / `model_response` / `execute` step 3 | After receiving the second render, the student reported people too distant and behind the guard, and the screen viewed from behind and too high. It moved the foreground figure, rebuilt the reaching pose, changed screen placement/orientation and used a more level camera while retaining machine parts. These are reported discrepancies and attempted corrections, not verified fixes. |
| Lines 26, 28–30, build/render/result/select | Third build and render completed with `ok: true`; step 3 was selected. There is no subsequent student comparison or `DONE` in the supplied trace. |

**Teacher and exploration.** No separate teacher diagnosis, proposed update or teacher receipt appears. The system supplied general reconstruction and verification instructions; the runner supplied each render and a request to compare or finish (lines 1, 11, 21). The student’s revisions show adoption of that feedback loop, not adoption of a specific teacher-authored diagnosis. Sessions reported no observable tool calls; the three externally executed builds constitute the visible autonomous iteration (lines 2, 12, 22; 4, 14, 24).

**Outcome and uncertainty.** This is a **technical build/render success with visual correctness unknown**, not an empty patch, execution failure or demonstrated formal scene success. The final image and reference are not visible in this audit. Consequently, actual object coverage, textures, pose, screen–hand contact, part connectivity, occlusion, camera match and lighting quality remain unverified. The program requested 32 samples, while render logs show 16; effective runner settings are not fully established (lines 24, 29). Whether the final camera and pose changes improved the match remains an unresolved hypothesis.

**Lessons.** Transferable: distinguish successful rendering from visual validation, and use rendered feedback to test framing hypotheses. Task-specific: the closer camera and screen/pose revisions address this student’s reported cleanroom discrepancies; their effectiveness cannot be generalized or confirmed here.
